body:
This doesn't look like a bug, as is indicated by the fact that it doesn't crash when deferred

This causes an infinite recursion as you trigger `_child_entered_tree`, then reparent, which triggers `_child_entered_tree`

This particular code doesn't look right to me, and you should probably have some kind of check to prevent calling `_reparent_node` like this

@AThousandShips thank you for your reply. I'd be happy to learn how the infinite recursion is being triggered or why it isn't a bug. It being an infinite recursion certainly sounds plausable, however, I am not sure, or simply don't understand why. I also updated the MRP to reflect some of my thoughts better (other container is now a sibling of the first container).

Some thoughts, why I think it is a bug:
- Why does it NOT crash when the added child has no children itself?
- Why does it NOT crash when the added child has only children which are NOT of type Control?
- If I reparent a control node (which has a Control child itself) from Container A to Container B (both containers are siblings) in the child_entered_tree of container A, why does it still crash? I don't see where an infinite recursion would occur, as the child_entered_tree should only be called once for container A, right?

Maybe I am also missing something. I'd be grateful for any information as to why this is occuring, even if it's not an engine bug. Thanks! :)

I will look at the new MRP, but the code in that MRP doesn't make sense where you change the parent after the node was reparented, it doesn't look like valid code, but I will test and see what the error log might be

There is an error in your logic. When you press ENTER, in the same frame you are adding a child (add_child) and doing reparent(). If you put a sleep or do what I did in the print, it will work. You are adding a child in the Node Reparenter and then you are doing reparent() in the v_box_container in the same frame. You have to use call_deferred or do what I did in the example. And this happens with a scene that has some children because of the overhead. It takes longer to instantiate a scene with children than an empty scene, that's why you don't have the error with the empty scene.

Thank you for your replies and the testing the issue again! That makes sense. So if I understand it correctly, one should never call `reparent` on a node that has been added to some other node in the same frame?

Still I wish there'd be some sort of error message at least to give users some sort of information they can work with/give them an idea how to fix their code.

> Thank you for your replies and the testing the issue again! That makes sense. So if I understand it correctly, one should never call `reparent` on a node that has been added to some other node in the same frame?
>

The error message "ERROR: Condition "!is_inside_tree()" is true." informs you that you were trying to reparent the instantiated scene without it being in the node tree yet. Why did this happen for the scene that had the button node as a child? I believe it is due to an overload, since the button is a node that is drawn on the screen, unlike the other scene that has no children. I would not say that you cannot add it in the same frame as I said before, but the codes I sent indicate this, since the codes are called in the next frame or postponed. Let's let the Godot GUI team answer you better and maybe they will even implement this error information so that the Godot user knows what they are doing wrong.
